body:
Today is a quiet day on the scanner: the opportunity finder returned zero arbitrage candidates across all 83 live contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket. That's the normal state of affairs — genuine cross-platform arbitrage in gold prediction markets is rare, and finding nothing simply means the two venues are pricing consistently once fees and thin order books are accounted for.

Gold itself is trading in the mid-$4,400s, and the market data lines up with that. JM Bullion's live feed puts spot at $4,419.37 as of Sep 08, 2026 at 11:13 AM EDT, while another tracker shows spot holding near $4,395, with silver at $65.88, as real yields climb and China's central bank extends its gold-buying streak. Kalshi's Sept 30, 2026 Above $4,410.99 contract is priced almost exactly at a coin-flip (bid 0.42 / ask 0.43), which is what you'd expect for a strike sitting right on top of the current spot. The broader run-up isn't new noise either: gold and silver enjoyed record-smashing rallies in 2025, surging 66% and 135% respectively over the course of the year, a move commentators tie to record inflows into gold-backed ETFs alongside strong bar and coin demand, even as official central-bank purchases have slowed.

One thing worth flagging for readers, not as an edge to trade but as a mechanics note: among Kalshi's far-dated Above $X strikes, the $4,370.99 strike (bid 0.53/ask 0.54) is quoted richer than the lower $4,330.99 strike (bid 0.49/ask 0.56), which shouldn't happen since a lower bar should always be at least as likely to clear. The $4,330.99 line has only 28 contracts of 24-hour volume versus 237 for its neighbor, so this looks like a stale, thinly-traded quote rather than free money — exactly the kind of book-depth issue the scanner's fill-size check is designed to screen out. Separately, Polymarket's contracts use a touch rule (did gold ever dip to a level during the window) while Kalshi settles on the spot price at a single expiry moment; that structural difference, not mispricing, explains why similarly-named contracts on the two platforms can show different-looking odds.
headline: Zero arbitrage found across 83 gold contracts as Kalshi and Polymarket price consistently
